title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食健康（人与自我·生活与健康·饮食与健康）
meta: 主题语境：饮食健康（人与自我·生活与健康·饮食与健康）　|　核心词汇：nut　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 nut 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1977 the baker ① cracked the nut that no customer in the bakery would have counted, and he said the cracking was the whole of the week. The ② nut, meaning the seed itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed uncounted in the book; a nut, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ nut in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ nut at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A nut, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the baker said the counting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the nut was the whole of the matter, meaning the strength and not the seed. The ⑥ nut, meaning the strength and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; nut, he said, is either something you crack or the only word that means both a seed and a strength. He said the strength is the part they remember.

By 1982 the ⑦ nut had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ nut of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of counting; nut, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ nut I remember is the seed counted in the bill, which closed in 1984 and is still counted as the quietest in the bakery. A ⑩ nut, my mother said in 1986, is the only seed that improves by being counted; every nut, she said, is a strength that has agreed to look like a seed. She said the strength was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 坚果；螺母（指糕饼铺里每一颗旁边的那一颗）
B. n. 坚果；螺母（指那颗坚果本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：crack the nut 砸这一颗坚果
D. n. 坚果；螺母（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 坚果之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的坚果之事）
F. n. 坚果；螺母（指账单里写到、被清点的那一颗）
G. n. 坚果、硬气（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 硬气（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: cracked the nut that no customer in the bakery would have counted
The nut, meaning the seed itself and not the tray
the nut at the far oven
the nut was the whole of the matter
the nut had become a line in a bill
The nut of the whole thing
A nut, my mother said in 1986

answers.why: crack the nut 意为“砸这一颗坚果”，1977 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯清点的一颗坚果做了一遍。
nut 意为“坚果；螺母”，指那颗坚果本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被清点。
nut 意为“坚果；螺母”，指糕饼铺里每一颗旁边的那一颗，每一颗旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
nut 意为“坚果；螺母”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
nut 意为“坚果、硬气”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这颗硬气就是那件事的全部。
nut 意为“硬气”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那颗坚果，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
nut 意为“坚果；螺母”，指账单里写到、被清点的那一颗，到 1982 年这一颗成了账单里的一行。
nut 意为“坚果之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的坚果之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的清点。
nut 意为“坚果；螺母”，我记得的是账单里清点过的那一颗，1984 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一颗。
nut 为抽象总称，母亲 1986 年说，坚果是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的坚果。
